420-program-description: Offered in Nunavik: practice skills with individuals, families and groups, with field training.
420-program-description-2: General practice in health and social services locally and abroad, using anti-oppressive frameworks. Builds professional identity, human rights, social justice, and critical thinking about systemic oppression and policy. Includes field practice.
420-field-practicum: Two days a week in U2 and U3, in different settings each year. U2 needs 24 credits, including all U1 required SWRK. U3 needs 54, including all U1 and U2 required SWRK.
421-about-sociology: The scientific study of society, giving tools to understand social forces, and preparing you for advanced study, management, education, law, medicine, social work and communications.
Minor, major, honours with a research paper, and joint honours. SOCI 210 is recommended, but usually not required for outsiders.
421-location: Leacock Building, Room 712, 855 Sherbrooke St. W.
421-advising: Advisers and schedules are on the Department's site.
421-program-description: A basic understanding of the field, expandable to the Major.
421-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3 from the list, and 9 from SOCI, at least 3 at 300+.
421-areas-of-sociology: Four areas: Institutions, Deviance and Culture; Politics and Social Change; Stratification (Class, Ethnicity, Gender); Work, Organizations and the Economy. 500-level seminars are for final-year social science majors and Honours; minors need permission.
422-program-description: A comprehensive understanding of the field.
423-u2-required-courses-6-credits: If exempt from SOCI 350, take another SOCI at 300+.
423-complementary-courses-24-credits: At least 3 at 400+, at most 9 at 200, at most 6 of current problems, independent study or reading. 500-level seminars in your final year.
424-program-description: More focus and depth, an asset for graduate or professional school. Register at the start of U2. Keep program GPA 3.50 and CGPA 3.00.
425-complementary-courses-30-credits: SOCI: at least 9 at 400+, at most 9 at 200. 500-level seminars in your final year.
426-program-description: More focus and depth, with another Arts discipline. Register at the start of U2, with an adviser in each. Keep program GPA 3.50 and CGPA 3.00.
426-complementary-courses-18-credits: SOCI approved by the Honours Adviser. 500-level seminars in your final year.
428-about-the-bachelor-of-arts-and-scien: Since September 2005, an interdisciplinary degree with roughly equal Arts and Science, through one from each faculty or a joint program like Sustainability or Cognitive Science.

Prepares you for jobs, business, law, medicine and graduate programs. It's for those committed to both sides, not a compromise for the undecided, who can take some of the other subject within a B.A. or B.Sc.
428-administrative-officers: The Associate Dean, Student Affairs (Science), is responsible for B.A. & Sc. students. The Program Administration Committee oversees curriculum and rules.
428-location: SOUSA: Frank Dawson Adams Building, Room 23, 3450 University St. It advises B.A. & Sc. and B.Sc. students.
428-prospective-high-school-and-cegep-ap: See Undergraduate Admissions. Review is by the central Admissions Office.
428-current-mcgill-students: See p. 39 and SOUSA for transfers.
429-degree-advising-and-sousa: The degree adviser, Tania Raggo, and SOUSA help with Foundation, planning, requirements, rules, exchange, exams, transfers and readmission, and support you through difficulties.
Special requests go in writing to the Associate Dean; the Committee on Student Standing hears appeals.
429-program-advising: In each department, not assigned. Ask about requirements, courses, registration problems, careers, graduate school and research.
429-choosing-a-b-a-sc-program: Follow one of the four program streams (p. 430).
429-preparation-for-graduate-school: Good for integrated fields like Cognitive or Environmental Science or Sustainability. For a specific arts or science graduate program, ask advisers here and there; 36-credit concentrations are less specialized than B.Sc. majors and honours.
429-first-year-advising: 120 credits with a mandatory Foundation Program. Advanced Standing can exempt parts, but you must meet all Foundation requirements.
U1 (96 or fewer to go): declare programs when registration opens, see a program adviser, and ideally a degree adviser. U0 (97–120): normally in Foundation; see a degree adviser.
430-degree-requirements: Your responsibility: know the rules and seek help from SOUSA; misunderstanding earns no exemption.
430-departmental-programs: Beyond Foundation, you need one approved stream: multi-track, joint honours, interfaculty or honours.
430-multi-track: A 90-credit program with a major concentration from each faculty.
430-regulations: Computer Science, Math and Statistics, and Psychology count as Science. Geography can be taken in both. 200+ prerequisites count within the 36. No course counts twice.
430-definitions: Major Concentration: 36–38 credits from a unit.
430-joint-honours-program: One component from Arts and one from Science, each at most 36 credits, or as few as 30 if 24 are honours-restricted. GPA rules are on p. 67.
430-regulations-2: Mathematics and Psychology count as Science. 200+ prerequisites count. No course counts twice.
430-interfaculty-program: An approved interfaculty concentration, with an optional minor. At least 21 credits each in Arts and Science.
431-regulations: At least 21 credits each in Arts and Science. No course counts twice.
431-honours-program: Specialized, preparing for graduate study, with an optional minor and at least 21 credits each in Arts and Science.
431-option-2: CGPA 3.00 at graduation, 3.50 for First Class. Some departments ask more. 30 credits of electives.
431-regulations-2: At least 21 credits each in Arts and Science, no double counting, GPA rules on p. 67.
431-minimum-credit-requirement: As in your admission letter, normally 120, with up to 30 Advanced Standing. Readmitted after five years, possibly 60 new credits and a new GPA, or fewer if approved. Otherwise, current requirements apply.
431-residency-requirement: 60 credits at McGill, not counting Foundation math and science. Two-thirds of each program too, not counting a prior McGill degree. Approved exchange can exempt with prior approval. Departments may require more.
431-time-and-credit-limit-for-completion: Eight terms with 96 or fewer to go; Foundation students start counting after a year. Requirements should fit within 120 credits.
Going beyond takes the Associate Dean's permission, normally for valid academic reasons such as a program change or part-time status, and only needed courses count.
431-course-requirements: C or better in program courses, including Foundation. If short: supplemental, extra work if offered, or repeat, normally once. A third try takes a written appeal; if refused, you must withdraw. A failed complementary can be replaced, with a D still counting as an elective. A repeated required D gives credit once.
Multi-track and Joint Honours students take BASC 201.
433-courses-in-english-as-a-second-langu: Up to 12 credits, if English isn't your primary language and you've had under five years of English secondary school.
433-courses-outside-the-faculties-of-art: At most 12 credits, or 30 in Environment and Sustainability programs and the Geography (Urban Studies) major. Continuing Studies courses don't count. Courses listed in Arts or Science sections count as theirs. Strictly enforced.
433-distance-education-courses: At most 6 credits, as electives, from accredited degree-granting schools with SOUSA's approval. Within your term maximum. For program requirements, only with serious documented reasons and prior approval.
434-registration-for-first-year-seminars: For first-year U0 or U1 students, first-come, 25 at most. Only one. Lists on p. 167.
434-overview-of-programs-offered: Review program structure on p. 430 first. Foundation is mandatory.
434-b-a-sc-foundation-program: For those with 97–120 credits to go. All must meet its requirements, unless admitted with a Québec DEC in Science or Integrated Arts and Science, even if admitted to U1. Its science may not satisfy all medical or dental schools. SOUSA has a planner.
434-program-description: For those with 97–120 credits to go. Check prerequisites for further study.
434-foundational-courses: Foundational courses in both Science and Arts.
434-math: At least two: at most one each of first calculus, second calculus and linear algebra.
435-science: At least three, with at most one first physics, one second physics (PHYS 101 before 102, 131 before 142), and two other foundational. CHEM 120 isn't open after CHEM 115. If COMP 202 or PSYC 100 is required by your program, use another course for Foundation.
435-arts: At least 9 credits in two of Humanities, Languages, Social Sciences; at most 6 per category and department. No course counts twice.
435-humanities-literature-and-civilizati: ARTH, COMS, CLAS, EAST, ENGL, FREN, GERM, HISP, ISLA, ITAL, JWST, MUAR, PHIL, RELG, RUSS.
435-languages: CLAS, EAST, CEAP, CESL, FRSL, FREN, GERM, HISP, ISLA, ITAL, JWST, RUSS.
436-advanced-standing-transfer-credits: DCS, AP, A-Levels, IB, French Baccalaureate, placement exams or other studies can exempt or give credit for math, science and Arts. Declare AP 4 or 5 when first registering. Choose math and science to meet your programs' prerequisites.
436-honours-programs: Three, each 60 credits, with extra GPA rules and a 6-credit research course.
436-interfaculty-programs: Three interdisciplinary programs across Arts and Science.
436-joint-honours-programs: One Arts and one Science component, registered for both, with an adviser in each. BASC 201 required. GPA rules apply.
437-major-concentrations: A 36-credit Arts Major, a 36–38 credit Science Major and BASC 201. An Arts major needs 30+ Arts credits; a Science one, 30+ Science credits.
437-faculty-of-arts-minor-concentrations: Includes GIS & Remote Sensing (p. 518) and Quebec Studies and Community-Engaged Learning (p. 541).
438-browse-academic-units-and-programs: A broad liberal education across McGill's two largest faculties. These units have approved programs for 2026–2027, including Quebec Studies (p. 541).
